doc.title: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack") Interview, 1959-07-01
doc.interviewee: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack")

title: The Baby Mac record, the move north in 1914 and T.O.B.A.
summary: Billy says he is not the Baby Mac on an Armstrong record. They went to Memphis in 1911, organized a company in New Orleans in 1914 and booked theaters directly to New York; he says they helped organize T.O.B.A. and played it as a singing, dancing, talking team.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: about then. Can you tell me more about your act? Just, I know you sang. All I know is the record that you made with Punch. And one other question I wanted to ask while I think of it. There was a record with Louis Armstrong. I tried to get every record that Armstrong ever made. And there was one with a Baby Mac singing. Now, was that you? That little Baby Mac. That wasn't me. No relation? No. No relation. No relation.
I wondered. Well, now, uh, uh, we, uh, uh, in 1914, that's the first time we supposed to come up north,

you know. We went to Memphis, Tennessee. Wasn't it, Matt? Yeah. No, we went to Memphis in 1911. 1911. But it was 1914 when we'd come back to New Orleans and organized this company. And then went to New York. Yes. And went everywhere along the lines, stopping in different towns. And at that time, we didn't have any booking agents. We'd just write to the theater managers that we could hear of. Book yourself directly. Just book direct all the way along from New Orleans to New York. Later, there was that T.O.B.A. were you ever on that? Oh, we stayed on that. We organized it, yeah. We really helped organize it. We knew, uh, Mr. Dudley, S.H. Dudley, and, uh, Mr. Sam Reaven of Chattanooga, Tennessee, and, uh, Mr. Klein, Martin Klein of Chicago. And Bailey. Yeah, Bailey in Atlanta. And Tim Osley of, uh, uh, Indianapolis, they got together to organize this and they first called it, uh, the, uh, uh, uh, Dudley-Dudley-Kline Circuit. But they later called it the Theater Owners Booking Association. Yes. And, uh, we were in there at all that. We did a vaudeville act for them around just a team, singing, dancing, and talking. Yeah.
